key_insight: The paper introduces an online shot-stopping framework that halts quantum circuit execution when extra shots stop meaningfully changing the empirical output distribution.
engineering_relevance: This can cut runtime and cost on noisy quantum hardware by using only the shots needed to reach a target distribution stability for static circuits.
method: IncrementalExecution monitors the evolving empirical distribution after each batch of shots.
It applies a point-of-diminishing-returns stopping rule to decide when to stop.
The framework allows customizable shot-management policies for different cost–fidelity trade-offs.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluated 33,750 framework configurations over 180 static circuit-backend combinations, totaling 7.3M independent experiments.
watch_item: The approach is designed for static black-box circuits, so its stopping policy may need retuning for highly dynamic workflows or when backend conditions drift.
paper_title: How Many Shots Are Enough for a Quantum Circuit?
